red_flag_claims.claim_text: OAS primarily targets defense, homeland security, and public safety customers. A significant portion of revenue depends on government customers.
red_flag_claims.M_check: USAspending federal contracts/grants for Ondas, Airobotics, American Robotics, Sentrycs, Roboteam (2020-2026)
red_flag_claims.M_value: Direct 'Ondas' substring matches = 10 awards / $206K, but ALL 10 are HONDASHOKAI Y.K. (a Japanese supplier — plywood, freezer boxes, flow meter calibration in Iwakuni). Zero awards to Ondas Inc., Ondas Holdings, Ondas Networks, Ondas Autonomous Systems. Airobotics: 0 contracts, 0 grants. Sentrycs: 0. Roboteam: 0. American Robotics: 1 DHS award ($167K) for 'UAS sniffer package'. Ondas grant hits are foreign-NGO substring noise (FONDASYON KOLE ZEPOL, etc.).
red_flag_claims.interpretation: Apply Layer 3 Rule 7 + Heuristic 9: company positions itself as a US-defense / homeland-security / public-safety contractor and explicitly tells investors that 'a significant portion of our business... involves sales to government customers, including defense, homeland security, and public safety agencies.' USAspending shows essentially zero federal contract obligations across the parent and every named acquired defense subsidiary (Airobotics, Sentrycs, Roboteam, 4M Defense). The only direct hit, American Robotics, has a single $168K DHS award — a rounding error relative to the ~$50M of revenue claimed for 2025 ($27.8M + $5.4M + smaller). HARD CONTRADICTION. The $27.8M anchor customer is therefore extremely unlikely to be a US federal defense buyer; if it is foreign or commercial, the marketing-vs-reality gap (military-base protection, mobile air defense, force protection, US DoD budgets) is material.

red_flag_claims.claim_text: Sentrycs (CoRF CUAS), Roboteam (UGV), 4M Defense (demining) are deployed defense capabilities feeding the US DoD / Western military customer base.
red_flag_claims.M_check: USAspending federal contracts for Sentrycs and Roboteam (2020-2026)
red_flag_claims.M_value: Sentrycs: 0 federal awards. Roboteam: 0 federal awards. (Both queried unrestricted by awarding agency — covers DoD, DHS, State, every federal buyer.)
red_flag_claims.interpretation: Per Heuristic 9: company markets Sentrycs and Roboteam as integrated CUAS/UGV defense platforms that can be deployed for 'defense, homeland security, and public safety customers' and ties them directly to US DoD spending ('U.S. defense budget surging to nearly $748 million for small unmanned systems in FY2026'). Zero federal contract obligations for either named subsidiary is a HARD CONTRADICTION on the stated US-defense positioning. Could reflect that these companies sell to Israel / UAE / foreign militaries (consistent with Israel HQ + UAE litigation footprint disclosed in legal proceedings) — but the 10-K's plain-language framing implies US-government customers. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE on the implied US-federal-customer scope; would moderate if framed as foreign-only.

severe_claims.claim_text: Ondas Networks has historically targeted North American freight rail (AAR, Class I railroads) as the early adoption market for FullMAX; industry bodies including AAR adopted IEEE 802.16.
severe_claims.M_check: EDGAR fulltext for 'FullMAX', 'Ondas Networks', '802.16t' across all filers and restricted to Class I railroads + Wabtec (the rail PTC vendor)
severe_claims.M_value: FullMAX total EDGAR hits = 168, all top hits are Ondas's own filings. Restricted to UP (CIK 0000100885) = 0 hits; CSX = 0; NSC = 0; BRK (parent of BNSF) = 0; Wabtec (the dominant rail PTC equipment OEM) = 0; CN = 0; CP/CPKC = 0. Ondas Networks total = 280 hits, all top hits are Ondas's own filings.
severe_claims.interpretation: Apply Heuristic 7 with caveat: railroads ARE the claimed end customer and FullMAX/AAR/802.16 deployment is the company's headline rail proof-point. A genuine Class I railroad rolling out FullMAX over a multi-year PTC/next-gen-comms program would typically appear in 10-K risk factors, capex disclosures, or vendor-concentration mentions; total absence across the five US Class I railroads and Wabtec (the prime integrator) suggests FullMAX has not achieved material commercial traction in the rail vertical despite being marketed as such since 2017+. This is similar to the LMT/NOC counterparty-silence pattern but stronger because the claim explicitly names the rail vertical as the lead adoption market. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY (not RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE because (a) some pilot/trial activity may exist below SEC-disclosure materiality and (b) AAR did publish 802.16 standards work, just not a deployed Ondas product).

moderate_claims.claim_text: Two customers accounted for $27.8M (55%) and $5.4M (11%) of 2025 revenue (vs. $3.8M / $1.9M / $0.7M for top 3 customers in 2024 — a 7x+ jump in concentration revenue), with one customer = 73% of A/R at year-end.
moderate_claims.M_check: EDGAR fulltext for 'Ondas', 'Airobotics', 'Optimus System' restricted to defense primes and Class I railroads
moderate_claims.M_value: Zero mentions across tested counterparty CIKs: LMT=0, NOC=0, RTX=0, GD=0, LHX=0, BA=0, UP=0, CSX=0, NSC=0, Berkshire=0, CN=0, CP/CPKC=0, Wabtec=0. Ondas EDGAR total 506 / Ondas Networks 280 / FullMAX 168 / Airobotics 119 / Optimus System 95 / Iron Drone Raider 107 — top hits in all searches are Ondas's own filings; no external filer surfaced. Anchor customer is undisclosed in 10-K, and no counterparty SEC filing corroborates Ondas as a vendor.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Apply Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold): a $27.8M relationship is generally NOT material to a Class I railroad ($25B-$30B revenue) or a top-5 defense prime ($30B-$70B revenue), so absence of mention there alone is not dispositive. However, combined with the 73% A/R concentration and revenue identity unknown, this is a watch item — particularly because (a) prior-year revenue concentration was sub-$4M largest customer and (b) the largest 2025 customer paid only a fraction of what was invoiced (73% A/R = ~$20M still outstanding). Score MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: the disclosure itself is the concern (collection risk + concentration), not yet a falsified claim.

severe_claims.claim_text: Teal selected as winner of U.S. Army SRR Program of Record (Nov 2024); FY2025 revenue growth attributed primarily to scaling drone deliveries under SRR program.
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts: Teal Drones 27 awards, $2.17M total; largest single award $750K (FA700025P0127 for 74 Teal 2 drones to USAFA/A3); no award description mentions 'Short Range Reconnaissance' or 'Program of Record'
usaspending.query_recipient_contracts: Red Cat Holdings 18 awards $3.79M total across DoD ($pieces), DHS, USDA, VA — bulk to non-DoD agencies
Award IDs are predominantly Air Force base-level FA-series purchase orders ranging $15K-$750K, plus Army National Guard small buys — not Program-of-Record IDIQ ceilings
severe_claims.M_check: usaspending.gov DoD obligations to all RCAT recipient name variants (Red Cat, Teal Drones, FlightWave, Red Cat Holdings, Skypersonic)
severe_claims.interpretation: RCAT claims FY2025 $40.7M revenue with ~73% from US Government (~$29.7M), primarily driven by SRR Program of Record scaling. USAspending shows only ~$4.9M of DoD obligations across ALL RCAT subsidiaries (Teal, FlightWave, Red Cat) and ~$7.0M including non-DoD federal — a ~4-6x gap vs. claimed government revenue. Per Heuristic 9 (DoD-CONTRACT-SPECIFIC): absence of SRR-named obligations for a company claiming an SRR Program of Record win is a hard contradiction. Could be explained by: (1) deliveries flowing through DLA/intermediaries not captured by recipient search; (2) IDIQ task orders not yet obligated; (3) sales to Defense Innovation Unit/Blue UAS Marketplace channel; or (4) genuine overstatement. Caveat: 2.5 page-result limit on top_awards may miss aggregation tail. The 27-award Teal total $2.17M is real, but $4.9M aggregate << $29.7M claimed. Severity: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY rather than RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE because some DoD presence exists and the program selection date (Nov 2024) is recent enough that ramp-up could lag obligation visibility — but the gap is large and SRR program-of-record awards should appear by FY2025 close.

severe_claims.claim_text: FY2025: ~73% of $40.7M revenue from US Government (~$29.7M).
supports: Sum of USAspending-traceable federal obligations to all RCAT subsidiaries: ~$7M lifetime, of which ~$4.9M is DoD
Even if all $4.9M DoD obligations to Teal+FlightWave+Red Cat had occurred in FY2025 alone (they did not — they accumulate 2020-2026), the figure is ~16% of claimed FY2025 US-Govt revenue
Concentration disclosure shows one customer = 73% of FY2025 revenue (Customer A: 88% of receivables) — consistent with single-program reliance
severe_claims.M_check: USAspending sum across recipient name variants; cross-check against 73% US-Govt revenue concentration disclosure
severe_claims.interpretation: Either claimed revenue substantially overstates real federal demand, OR USAspending recipient-name search materially undercounts via (a) prime-sub flow-throughs where RCAT is a subcontractor not the named recipient (NDAA/Blue UAS purchases via large primes); (b) sales through DIU's Blue UAS Marketplace where final recipient may be a procurement office aggregator; (c) Foreign Military Sales not in USAspending. Customer A at 73% revenue is consistent with a single Program-of-Record buyer — but that buyer's purchases should appear as obligations. This is the same divergence pattern as C1 — sized at fiscal-year resolution. Severity: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY.

Total FlightWave obligations ($2.3M) is modest relative to $14M purchase price and $8.7M ascribed goodwill
Acquisition was Sept 2024; some obligations may post-date acquisition
moderate_claims.M_check: usaspending DoD obligations to FlightWave (recipient substring)
moderate_claims.interpretation: FlightWave's DoD presence is real but modest ($2.3M lifetime). Ascribing $8.7M of goodwill to 'approved vendor' relationships with 'several US government agencies' is a soft claim — the actually-traceable federal contracting footprint is small. Not a hard contradiction (federal relationship exists), but ratio of goodwill to demonstrable revenue history is high. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY.

Jaunt Carter Aviation contingent payable: $44.6M converted to 1,122,437 shares + $5M cash at IPO
Coastal Defense (CDI) Promissory Note: $2.0M cash + 203,707 shares
Agile Defense, AIRO Drone notes converted at IPO (modest)
Investor Notes: notes accrue interest at 100%, 115%, 125%, 150% of principal payable in stock at Closing
M_value.material_weaknesses_disclosed: CEO/CFO concluded disclosure controls NOT effective as of 12/31/25; material weaknesses unremediated since FY2023; cited 'lack of sufficient personnel with appropriate accounting knowledge' and lack of precision in review controls over complex transactions
M_value.audit_history: Auditor BPM LLP since 2022; opined fair presentation but explicitly not engaged on ICFR
M_value.going_concern: Mgmt asserts sufficient liquidity for 12 months; $74.6M cash; FY2025 op cash flow = -$32.4M (vs +$21.5M FY2024); 79% of revenue concentrated in 2 customers

red_flag_claims.interpretation: Cluster of generic distress fingerprints from Memory's stock-for-services-as-distress-flag rubric: vendor payables converted to equity at IPO across multiple subsidiaries (Jaunt, Aspen, Coastal Defense, Agile Defense, AIRO Drone), 20% of subsidiary EBITDA payable to a stockholder via 'incentive agreement', and investor notes accruing interest at PRINCIPAL-multiple rates (100-150% in stock). Combined with: (a) UNREMEDIATED material weaknesses in ICFR since FY2023, (b) operating cash flow swing from +$21.5M (2024) to -$32.4M (2025), (c) 79% customer concentration in the Drones segment, (d) Electric Air Mobility segment generated $0 revenue in 2025 despite $7.6M R&D, (e) accumulated deficit $210.6M against $90.9M revenue, (f) goodwill $571.7M = 74% of total assets, never tested by company itself for impairment in 2025 (vs $38.0M impairment in 2024). Per Memory's 'divergence is not solvency' caveat: this scoring is on disclosure-quality risk, not a directional bet on operational distress. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE flagged for control-environment + dilutive-equity-payment patterns that warrant tier-1 forensic-accounting follow-up before underwriting.
